name: TS5A23159RSER
title: 1 Ω dual SPDT analog switch, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: Two independent single-pole double-throw CMOS switches, each a bidirectional 2:1 multiplexer or demultiplexer, running from one supply of 1.65 V to 5.5 V. On resistance is 0.7 Ω typical at 4.5 V, channel matching is tight, and the switch breaks before it makes. The control inputs take up to 5.5 V at any supply, and the analog ports stay isolated with the supply at 0 V. TS5A23159RSER is the 1.5 mm × 2 mm UQFN part; the same part also comes in a 3 mm × 3 mm VSSOP (DGS).

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A system controller on a 3.3 V rail sets both switch positions through IN1 and IN2 and passes signals on COM1 and COM2. Each channel connects its COM either to Port 1 through NC1 and NC2 (IN low) or to Port 2 through NO1 and NO2 (IN high). The switch and the controller each have a 0.1 µF capacitor from the 3.3 V rail to ground.
notes: U2's pin names are placeholders for the controller's two switch-control outputs and two signal lines.

circuits.title: ON-state resistance (Ron)
circuits.description: A selector puts a DC source on NC or NO, IN is driven to VIH or VIL to close that channel, and a current sink draws ICOM out of COM. Ron is the voltage across the switch, VCOM less VNO or VNC, divided by ICOM.
notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.

circuits.title: OFF-state leakage current
circuits.description: A selector puts a DC source on NC or NO and a second source holds COM, with IN at VIH or VIL so the channel under test is open. The current into the open port measures INC(OFF), INO(OFF) and their power-off counterparts; the same set-up measures COM leakage.
notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.

circuits.title: ON-state leakage current
circuits.description: A selector puts a DC source on NC or NO, IN at VIH or VIL closes that channel, and COM is left open at VCOM. The leakage of the closed path gives ICOM(ON), INC(ON) and INO(ON).
notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.

circuits.title: Capacitance
circuits.description: A capacitance meter biased at VBIAS (V+ or GND) is switched in turn to NC, NO, COM and IN, with IN at V+ or GND, to measure CI, CCOM(ON) and the NC and NO capacitances with the channel on and off.

parts.value: Capacitance meter, VBIAS = V+ or GND

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.
VI = V+ or GND.

circuits.title: Turnon and turnoff time (tON, tOFF)
circuits.description: COM is held at VCOM = V+; NC and NO each drive RL = 50 Ω and CL = 35 pF to ground. A logic pulse on IN switches the channel; tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the logic edge to the 90% point of the switch output.

parts.note: pulse generator, PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns, tf < 5 ns

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.
The repetition rate reads PRR 3 10 MHz; it should read PRR ≤ 10 MHz.

circuits.title: Break-before-make time (tBBM)
circuits.description: NC and NO are tied together to VNC = VNO = V+, and COM drives RL = 50 Ω and CL = 35 pF to ground. As IN changes over, VCOM dips while neither side conducts; tBBM is the time between the two 90% crossings of that dip.

parts.note: pulse generator, PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns, tf < 5 ns

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.
The repetition rate reads PRR 3 10 MHz; it should read PRR ≤ 10 MHz.

circuits.title: Bandwidth (BW)
circuits.description: A network analyzer's 0 dBm source (632 mV p-p into 50 Ω, 350 mV DC bias) drives NC through 50 Ω; COM returns to the analyzer's 50 Ω input. IN at V+ or GND closes NC to COM; BW is where the gain falls 3 dB below its DC value.

parts.value: Network analyzer source, 0 dBm, DC bias 350 mV

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.
NO is left unconnected.

circuits.title: Off isolation (OISO)
circuits.description: The analyzer's 0 dBm source drives NC through 50 Ω, with 50 Ω from NC to ground; COM goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input. IN at V+ or GND opens NC to COM and the analyzer reads what passes.

parts.value: Network analyzer source, 0 dBm, DC bias 350 mV

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.
NO is left unconnected.

circuits.title: Crosstalk (XTALK)
circuits.description: The analyzer's 0 dBm source drives NC through 50 Ω with NC to COM closed and COM loaded by 50 Ω to ground; NO, open to COM, goes to the analyzer's 50 Ω input, which reads the signal coupled across.

parts.value: Network analyzer source, 0 dBm, DC bias 350 mV

notes: Channel 1 stands for either channel.

circuits.title: Charge injection (QC)
circuits.description: A source VGEN (0 to V+) behind RGEN = 0 holds NC or NO; COM is loaded by CL = 1 nF. A logic pulse on IN switches the channel off, on and off, and the step ΔVCOM left on COM, times CL, is the injected charge.

where.VNO or VNC: voltage at the closed NO or NC port

equations.note: IN at VIH or VIL with the channel on.

where.ΔVCOM: step in the COM voltage caused by switching IN

operation.text: Each channel has its own control: IN low closes COM to NC and opens NO; IN high closes COM to NO and opens NC. The open side opens before the other closes, so NC and NO are never briefly joined.
NO, NC and COM conduct both ways, so any of them can be an input or an output. Analog and digital signals from 0 to VCC pass; the channel's −3 dB point is about 100 MHz at 5 V.

IN1 and IN2 tolerate 5.5 V whatever VCC is (recommended range 0 to VCC). VIH min is 2.4 V at 5 V, 2 V at 3.3 V, 1.8 V at 2.5 V and 1.5 V at 1.8 V supplies. A control pin left floating can set an unwanted position; give each a pull-up to VCC or a pull-down to GND, and tie unused digital inputs to one rail or the other.
With VCC = 0 the switch ports stay high impedance: power-off leakage on NC, NO or COM is ±1 µA max at 25°C (±20 µA over temperature with 5.5 V on the ports).

Bring VCC up before any voltage reaches NO, NC or COM, and stay inside the absolute maximum ratings. A bypass capacitor is not required; 0.1 µF from VCC to GND suits most designs and keeps switching noise off the supply.
The part needs no external components. Unused NO, NC or COM pins may be tied to ground through 50 Ω so signals are not reflected into the part.

Rpeak is the highest on resistance over the analog range; ΔRon the difference in Ron between the channels of one device; Ron(flat) the spread between the highest and lowest Ron of one channel over the stated conditions. Bandwidth is the frequency at which an on channel's gain is 3 dB under its DC gain. Off isolation is the signal through an open channel and crosstalk the signal coupled from an on channel into an off one, both in dB at a given frequency. THD is the RMS of the second and higher harmonics over the fundamental.

Keep traces short and wide to cut stray inductance and capacitance, put the bypass capacitor as close to the part as possible, and use large ground planes. A recommended layout puts the bypass capacitor at VCC (pin 8) with vias to the power and ground planes, and runs each signal pin straight out to the system.
